niches.rationale: Homeschooling parents who must record attendance days and instructional hours for their state or district: Many homeschool families need a simple recurring record of days and hours, and they buy printable logs fresh every school year.

niches.keyword: vehicle maintenance log printable oil change tire rotation
niches.rationale: Car owners and new drivers who want one place to record service dates, mileage, and repair history: Every car owner has recurring maintenance needs, so the search is evergreen and buyers look for a specific, practical record they can keep in the glovebox.

niches.keyword: houseplant watering and fertilizing log printable
niches.rationale: Indoor plant owners with a growing collection who want to track watering, feeding, and repotting dates per plant: Plant collections keep growing and buyers search for plant-specific tracking sheets that are simple, printable, and useful all year.

niches.keyword: moving day checklist printable room by room
niches.rationale: Renters and homeowners preparing for a move who want a room-by-room list of tasks, packing progress, and utility changes: Moving is a stressful, recurring life event with steady year-round search volume, and buyers look for printable room-by-room checklists to stay organized.

Freshwater and saltwater fish keepers who test pH, ammonia, nitrite, nitrate, and temperature and want to track changes over time: Aquarium owners test water on a regular schedule and need a place to record readings and water changes, which creates repeat demand from a passionate hobby community.

Home bakers who maintain a sourdough starter and want to record feeding times, flour ratios, and rise activity: Sourdough hobbyists search for tools that help them troubleshoot and keep a consistent starter, and a dedicated feeding log is a small, specific, evergreen need.

K-12 teachers preparing for planned or unexpected absences who want a consistent handoff for substitutes: Teachers buy printables every school year, and a ready-to-fill sub checklist saves time during stressful last-minute absences.

Small-scale landlords and Airbnb hosts tracking repairs, contractor visits, and upkeep dates per unit: Landlords need organized records of repairs and service dates, it's an evergreen need, and buyers search by this exact phrase.

Dog owners managing daily pills, supplements, or flea and heartworm preventatives for one or more pets: Pet owners with senior or chronic-condition dogs need a simple way to avoid missed or double doses, and the search phrase is specific with a clear purchase intent.

cycles.memo: Over the last 30 days we've earned $0.00 in revenue against $0.039 of LLM spend, so profit is about -$0.04. Spend is tiny, but there is no revenue signal yet, so I can't say whether the Etsy approach works. This cycle Etsy reviewed 3 listings and gave all 3 a 'keep' verdict (none scale, none kill). That is a weak verdict because no sales data backs it up. Etsy designed 2 new products and queued 2 listings, but 2 approvals are waiting on you, and nothing can go live or get pinned until you clear them. Pinterest queued 0 pins because no active listing with a URL needs one, so it is blocked on Etsy and its $0.0675 allocation will probably go unused. I allocated the most budget to Etsy ($0.3825 of $0.50) because it is the only team that can produce something sellable, and the total is small enough that the downside is negligible. Next cycle, watch whether the approved listings get any views, favorites, or sales. With zero sales so far, the sample is far too small to draw conclusions about niches or designs.
